newsitem.title: USA: Staples CEO confident deal will go through.
newsitem.headline: Staples CEO confident deal will go through.

text.p: Staples Inc chairman Tom Stemberg said OfficeMax Inc is getting "bargain basement" prices for the 63 outlets Staples and Office Depot Inc agreed to sell OfficeMax in an effort to gain government approval of their $4 billion merger.
Stemberg said the 63 stores "are doing business at a rate of about $6 million a year."
"Typically stores like that are sold for between $3 million and $4 million (each). We are selling for one and 3/4 million," he said.
"So I am not jumping up and down about the price. However, in the greater scheme of things, it was acceptable," he said after a presentation at a Merrill Lynch retailing conference.
"I am very optimistic that the deal will get done one way or another," Stemberg said adding that he feels Staples and Office Depot would prevail in a legal battle with the Federal Trade Commission.
He said the agreement to sell the stores to OfficeMax, a move designed to appease the FTC, was done "to end uncertainty."
On Monday, the commission rejected the merger, first announced last September.
"We are very hopeful not because we necessarily share their concern about pricing levels, (but) it would be fair to say...this would certainly address (the FTC concerns)," Stemberg said.
